title: Weather and changing conditions
moduleTitle: Group (Exterior, height & access): Methods and technique
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Identify safety and authorisation decisions associated with weather and changing conditions.
Explain the applicable risk hierarchy and specialist responsibilities for weather and changing conditions.
Produce a defensible stop-work, competent-person referral or restricted handover using mock evidence.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Purpose and assessable outcome
instruction.body: The learner must recognise dynamic weather assessment in the context of weather and changing conditions, identify evidence gaps, and prepare a safe decision record. Trainer distinguishes observation, inference and approval.

instruction.heading: Authorised scope and information needed
instruction.body: Review fictional work orders, site controller details, current method approval and the location-specific risk assessment. Require documented monitoring and the approved site-specific suspension process; avoid universal wind or storm limits. Document missing information as an open decision, not implicit permission.

instruction.heading: Hazard and safer-option analysis
instruction.body: Analyse the lesson case: Forecast wind and lightning risks change after the initial access plan was signed. Start with avoiding elevated work and select no method until competency, protection of third parties and site constraints are established. Escalate uncertainties before dispatch.

instruction.heading: Role boundaries and stop-work decision
instruction.body: Recommended decision: Stop the affected operation and obtain an updated competent-person decision; never invent universal weather limits. General cleaning training cannot sign off rope descent, platform operation, anchor certification, electrical clearance or emergency rescue capability.

instruction.heading: Evidence, communication and quality
instruction.body: Use dated simulated records to show the exact observation, source document, person notified, time, restriction and requested response. Refer to course research ha94-uk-window; do not claim a jurisdiction is approved.

instruction.heading: Trainer-led tabletop practice
instruction.body: Compare simulated forecast updates against a site-specific approved suspension trigger register. Use photographs, drawn plans, fictitious work orders and inert desk materials only. Trainer checks accuracy and intervenes if the learner proposes unauthorised real-world activities.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Confirm that documented monitoring is in place for the job and that the approved site-specific suspension process is available.
Compare each forecast change against the approved site suspension trigger register. Do not rely on universal wind or storm limits.
Record any missing information as an open decision, not as implied permission to proceed.
Stop the affected operation when conditions change.
Escalate to the site controller or competent person, and obtain an updated competent-person decision before work resumes.
Do not sign off rope descent, platform operation, anchor certification, electrical clearance or emergency rescue capability on the basis of general cleaning training.
Record the observation, the source document, the person notified, the time, the restriction and the response requested.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed below that (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: Documented monitoring is in place for the job.
Forecast changes are compared against the approved site suspension trigger register.
The affected operation stops when conditions change, and no universal weather limit is assumed.
An updated competent-person decision is obtained before work resumes.
summary: Weather and changing conditions are monitored against the site-specific suspension process, and the access plan is reviewed when forecasts change.
Universal wind or storm limits are not invented, and the approved site trigger register is used instead.
When conditions change, the affected operation stops and an updated competent-person decision is obtained.

knowledgeChecks.question: For weather and changing conditions, what evidence must be established before allocating work, and which facts are still unverified?
options: A universal wind limit taken from the internet
Documented monitoring and a suspension process
The original access plan, still signed and valid
The worker's feeling that conditions are fine

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say about wind and storm limits?
options: Use a universal wind limit from the internet
Ignore the weather once the plan is signed
Use the worker's feeling about the conditions
Avoid universal wind or storm limits, and use documented monitoring and the approved site-specific suspension process
